applicabilityConditions: The Workbench predicate ID must be CLOSES or CLOSED.
The source construction must express the active transitive close sense: subject is the agent and object is the entity whose openness changes.
Both subject and object must resolve to explicit referents; an unresolved pronoun, missing object, or unknown filler does not satisfy this mapping.

The subject must be known to satisfy the Python frame role class Agent, and the object must be known to satisfy Artifact (or a class accepted as its subclass by the Python ontology). Unknown entity types produce PARTIAL/UNRESOLVED compatibility, not an exact mapping.
No additional semantically material source arguments may be discarded. They must be mapped by a separate approved rule or cause PARTIAL compatibility.
Polarity, modality, quantifier scope, tense, aspect, attribution, temporal information, evidence, and provenance are outside this predicate-frame mapping and must be handled by their own mappings.
semanticBasis: Python CLOSE@1 specializes STATE_CHANGE@1. It inherits the AGENT role from STATE_CHANGE and narrows UNDERGOER to Artifact; UNDERGOER is required.
CLOSE@1 pins the changed dimension to Openness, direction to DECREASE, and target value to ClosedState.
Workbench v0.5.4 classifies CLOSES/CLOSED as event predicates and requires subject/object roles for these transitive predicates.
nonCoverage: This mapping does not cover intransitive or middle uses such as 'The door closed' because the current Workbench transitive argument contract does not identify the same role structure.
This mapping does not by itself convert the surrounding USG-SEM expression tree or document metadata.

nonMappings.reason: The Python 0.4.0 frame catalogue has no frame whose defined semantics represent needing. Reusing a generic state frame would assert a meaning the target frame does not define.
The frame catalogue has no exact liking/positive-preference frame. Do not map by broad similarity to ATTITUDE or EXPERIENCE_STATE.
The frame catalogue has no exact disliking/negative-preference frame. ALLERGIC and other experience-state frames have different meanings.

Python WANT@1 requires CONTENT of kind EVENT. The current Workbench predication represents its object as an entity argument, not an event-valued content expression. A direct entity-to-CONTENT conversion would be a kind error.

Python KNOW@1 and BELIEVE@1 require proposition-valued CONTENT. The current Workbench PREDICATION object slot is an entity referent, not a proposition. A mapping needs an explicit embedded proposition, not a surface object.

Python COMMERCIAL_TRANSACTION@1 requires BUYER, SELLER, and GOODS. The current Workbench subject/object structure supplies at most two arguments, and the subject role differs between buy and sell perspectives. ACQUIRE is also broader than purchase. No full mapping is approved; missing parties must not be invented.

The Python GIVE@1 frame can express a recipient perspective, but the Workbench receive predication supplies recipient and theme without the required transfer AGENT/SOURCE. It may be explored as a partial candidate later, but it is not an exact mapping.

STATE_CHANGE@1 is not a generic synonym frame. It requires a defined change dimension and has direction/target-value semantics. These Workbench predicates do not consistently provide the exact dimension, initial/final state, or target-value information needed for a lossless mapping.
The frame catalogue has no exact START or FAIL frame. Mapping either to generic STATE_CHANGE or ATTEMPT would alter or overstate the source meaning.
No frame in the Python 0.4.0 foundation expresses the same use/stop-using predication with an exact role contract.
No CREATE/PRODUCE event frame exists in the Python 0.4.0 frame catalogue. Do not substitute a generic transformation or information-processing frame.
The frame catalogue has no exact measurement frame and the Workbench predicate does not establish the required measurement instrument, quantity, or result semantics.

These are relation predicates, not a homogeneous event-frame family. They require a separate relation/operator mapping. In particular, CAUSATION@1 relates propositions, while the current relation predicates may carry entity arguments.
These predicates require property/identity/existence semantics rather than a frame match. Their conversion belongs in a separate predicate-to-expression/operator mapping.

The identifier CLOSE appears in the Workbench transitive-argument vocabulary but is not included in its event-predicate classification set. It is not covered by the CLOSES/CLOSED mapping until the source predicate classification is made consistent.

policy.unknownPredicateBehavior: Never select a frame by lexical similarity. Return UNSUPPORTED.
policy.unmetApplicabilityBehavior: Return PARTIAL or UNRESOLVED with the failed conditions; do not claim EXACT compatibility.
policy.semanticLossBehavior: Never drop, flatten, invent, or silently coerce an argument or semantic operator.
policy.versioning: Treat each published registry version as immutable. Add or change mappings only with source evidence, tests, and a new registry version.
